thread:
jin: quick q — pushed a config-only change to infra repo (logging default tweak). deploy-bot ran and created a candidate. should we bump patch (v1.4.2 -> v1.4.3) or mark as meta and avoid semver bump?
release-bot: Deploy check ok — no compiled code changed, only config. no schema diffs detected. :robot_face:
morgan: if it affects customer-observed behavior, bump. if it's internal defaults, can batch non-user-visible into a weekly patch. :calendar:
owen: +1 to batching but tags are important for rollbacks. if we don't bump patch, tools that sort by semver might ignore this update.
aliya: our release-notes generator grabs commits with `release: patch` footer. we could introduce `release: meta` but tooling doesn't treat it specially yet.
matt: i lean patch. keeps support simple — easier to point to a patch that included the change. patches are cheap.
danielle: worried about churn — if we bump for every micro-config the patch number inflates. maybe use a `meta` annotated tag like:
```n.git tag -a v1.4.3-meta.1 -m "meta: logging default tweak"
git push origin v1.4.3-meta.1
```
jin: what would rollback look like if we land meta tags? can't rely on semver increment to drive rollback if we avoid patch bumps.
owen: rollback is by deployed tag via deploy-bot, so a clear meta tag is fine. but dashboards that rollup by major/minor/patch may misclassify meta releases.
morgan: ops suggestion — use `release: skip` in commit footer for things we don't want in release notes and only bump patch for changes that affect API/UX/perf.
jin: proposal: infra-only defaults use `release: skip` and we batch into a weekly "infra-meta" release with tags like `v1.4.3-infra.1`. anything customer-facing bumps patch. objections?
aliya: no objections. i'll update CONTRIBUTING.md and add snippet so release-bot ignores `release: skip`.
matt: sounds good. :thumbsup:
release-bot: noted. will add a filter for `release: skip` on the next deploy cycle.
danielle: can we add a short console changelog flag for "infra-meta" items so support isn't surprised? a one-line banner should do it.
jin: thanks — i'll draft the doc and ping infra-owner to start the weekly bundle.
